comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C7-C10 regarding mammary epithelial phenotypes, ductal hyperplasia, and tumorigenesis. Both evaluations find the evidence solid and convincing with no methodological concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C62-C68 regarding CRB3-Rab11-GCP6 interactions. Both accept the co-IP and domain mapping data, though peer reviewers note the precise mechanism 'remains to be clarified' while OpenEval finds the evidence fully supportive.
Strong agreement on claims C23-C32 regarding reduced ciliation frequency in CRB3-depleted cells. Both evaluations accept the rescue experiments and find the ciliogenesis data solid and convincing.
Strong agreement on claims C13-C20 regarding impaired acinar morphogenesis in 3D cultures. Both evaluations find the cellular phenotype data solid with no concerns raised about methodology.

Divergent evaluations on claims C70-C73 regarding the vesicle targeting mechanism. OpenEval finds the evidence supportive, while peer reviewers rate it as UNCERTAIN, noting that 'the precise mechanism remains to be clarified' and the navigator model (C73) requires further validation.
Strong agreement on claims C35-C40 regarding CRB3 localization to the ciliary base. Both evaluations accept the localization data using multiple markers without critique.

Strong agreement on claims C42-C52 regarding Rab11-dependent trafficking mechanisms. Both evaluations accept the mass spectrometry, co-localization, and pharmacological manipulation data as supporting the vesicle trafficking model.
Agreement on claims C55-C60 regarding CRB3's role in γ-TuRC assembly. Both evaluations accept the biochemical evidence showing disrupted interactions without changes in expression levels.
Agreement on claims C78-C85 regarding differential effects on Hedgehog and Wnt signaling pathways. Both evaluations accept the signaling data across multiple experimental systems.

Agreement on claims C4-C6 regarding perinatal lethality and anophthalmia phenotypes. Both evaluations find these observations solid and convincing. OpenEval additionally evaluates C1-C3 (construction strategy and genotyping) which peer reviewers do not explicitly address.
Agreement on claims C74-C77 regarding observations in human breast cancer tissues. Both evaluations accept these clinical observations as part of the broader evidence linking CRB3 to tumorigenesis.

Partial overlap on claims C100-C101 regarding the integrative model. OpenEval finds C99-C102 fully supported as a coherent synthesis, while peer reviewers (R12) rate the overall mechanism as UNCERTAIN, noting it requires further clarification despite supporting evidence.

Partial overlap on claims C133-C136 regarding comprehensive summary of findings. OpenEval finds the synthesis well-supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about the precise mechanism, though they accept the individual components.

OpenEval evaluates claims C86-C91 regarding additional phenotypes (polarity defects, lumen filling) with supporting evaluation, noting some data are not shown. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims C92-C98 regarding reconciliation of CRB3 localization discrepancies in the literature. These methodological clarifications are not explicitly addressed in peer review.
